answer: Register one apiary in a meadow above the ocean and prove the bees exist. A county officer bolts a numbered plate to 12 hives at 180 dollars each, a sliver of opal set into each plate and photographed with a loupe. Over 90 days the keeper files 12 notes, each with a fresh photo of the plate and a honey weight, signed by a neighbor. A forged log costs a 250 token deposit and the license for a year. A hive register works like a boat log: catches are dated and signed, so a boat that never leaves the harbor cannot fake a season of fish, and a keeper with no bees cannot fake a season of honey.
